threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot newcomers by their bewildered faces at the Overground delays—while the rest of us just roll our eyes and carry on.
Saw a guy in a full tuxedo on the 333 last night, talking to a takeaway cart like it was his date. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw my neighbor arguing with a pigeon over a piece of bread on the sidewalk. Just another Sunday in the Kiez.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a full-on dance party at a weekday street market, with locals mixing it up between stalls and old-school techno beats.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can always spot a local by how they navigate BART delays without a second thought—just another Tuesday for us, right?

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today with a guy playing the ukulele in the back. He turned the cramped ride into a mini concert, had everyone smiling despite the delays.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think everyone speaks English here. Try ordering at a bar with a heavy accent; you'll see the locals’ true expressions!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a newcomer by their wide-eyed wonder at the Plaça del Sol, clutching a map like it’s a treasure map.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it ‘the tube’ instead of ‘the Underground’ like a true local. It’s a dead giveaway.
I saw a guy serenading a pigeon on the 133 last night; the bird looked genuinely confused. Only in Brixton, I guess.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid ride a unicycle past the Döner shop while their grandma argued with the butcher about the best meat for Kebab. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a bar that offers ping pong tournaments while serving craft beer brewed on-site—tucked behind a graffiti-covered wall.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know to avoid BART delays by taking the bus, even if it’s labeled the most delayed. We’ve got our strategies.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today where a guy serenaded the whole ride with a ukulele. Not sure if it made the delays better or worse, but we were all smiling.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's just about Gaudí and bars, but on a Sunday morning, the real vibe is families at the plaça and kids chasing pigeons.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their over-excitement at finding a 'hidden' tapas bar that everyone in Gràcia has been to at least twice.
